title: Numbers
author: Moses is traditionally understood as the author of Numbers as part of the Pentateuch.
date: Traditionally connected with Israel's wilderness wanderings before entering the promised land.
audience: Israel, especially the generation preparing to enter the promised land, warning them against unbelief and calling them to trust the Lord.
historicalSetting: Numbers records Israel's journey from Sinai through the wilderness toward Canaan. It includes censuses, rebellion, judgment, wilderness wandering, and preparation for entrance into the land.
keyVerse: Numbers 6:24-26 — "Yahweh bless you, and keep you. Yahweh make his face to shine on you, and be gracious to you. Yahweh lift up his face toward you, and give you peace."
christFocus: Numbers points to Christ through God's provision in the wilderness, the bronze serpent lifted up for healing, the faithful mediator, and the hope of God's blessing and presence. Christ is the One lifted up that all who look to Him in faith may live.
outline: Preparation and census at Sinai — Numbers 1-10
Complaining, rebellion, and judgment in the wilderness — Numbers 11-20
The bronze serpent, Balaam, and wilderness victories — Numbers 21-25
The new generation counted and instructed — Numbers 26-30
Preparation for the land and final instructions — Numbers 31-36
